about.heroDescription: We are a cooperative of people who organise trips in Mongolia and share the income more fairly.
about.story1: Sain Sanaa began as an idea of Alfredo Savino, a long-standing member of the Soyombo Association, lecturer in Italian at the National University of Mongolia and trip organiser: to create a cooperative of people who organise trips in Mongolia, to share more fairly the resources that tourism brings every summer.
about.story2: In recent years Mongolia has had a tourism boom, but the wealth benefits only a few agencies which, to stay competitive, pay very low wages to the people who actually make it possible to visit the country. Sain Sanaa chose a new, against-the-grain path: better services and more fairness.
about.story3: Each member shares their knowledge and skills to draw up new, little-travelled itineraries. Travellers meet a truer Mongolia, away from the classic tourist circuits, and also help the most remote communities.

sections.title: Visa and documents
items: You need a valid passport, with at least six months of remaining validity and at least two blank pages.

The visa can be requested online at evisa.mn: you need a digital scan of your passport and a passport-style photo, a credit card, and the name and number of an emergency contact. The cooperative has quoted a cost of about 50 euros in the past.
Alternatively you can request the visa at the Mongolian Embassy in Rome (original documents, on average 7–10 days to issue, with a double fee for urgent requests).

Rules and costs change often: always check the Italian foreign ministry travel advice (“Viaggiare Sicuri”) and the embassy before you leave. We also confirm the current situation when you write to us.

sections.title: Travel insurance
items: We recommend travel health insurance with medical assistance and repatriation: outside Ulaanbaatar hospitals are far away.
Many of our travellers have been happy with Heymondo. Always check that the cover includes the activities in your programme, such as horse riding and trekking, and your luggage.
Keep the policy’s assistance number and a copy of the contract with you.

sections.title: Getting there
items: Most people fly to Ulaanbaatar (Chinggis Khaan International Airport), usually with a connection in Europe or Asia.
The alternative is the train: the Trans-Mongolian line links Ulaanbaatar with Beijing and the Trans-Siberian railway.
The time difference with Italy is 6 hours in summer and 7 in winter; Mongolia has no daylight saving time.

sections.title: Climate and what to pack
items: The climate is continental: summers are hot by day and cool at night, winters are very cold. The best season is usually June to September; Naadam takes place in mid-July.
Dress in layers: a windproof, waterproof jacket, a fleece, comfortable boots, a hat, sunglasses and sunscreen.
Useful extras: a sleeping-bag liner, a head torch, a power bank, flip-flops for camps and your personal medicines.

sections.title: Health
items: Talk to your doctor or a travel-medicine clinic at least 4–6 weeks before you leave.
Drink only bottled or boiled water. Bring a supply of your usual medicines.
In remote areas help can take time: tell your guide about any health problem.

sections.title: Money and connectivity
items: The currency is the tögrög (MNT). Cards work in Ulaanbaatar; in the countryside you need cash. ATMs are in Ulaanbaatar and provincial capitals.
Local SIM cards are easy to buy in town. Coverage is good in towns and poor in remote areas.
Mains power is 230 V with type C and E sockets: usually an adapter is all you need.

sections.title: Safety
items: Mongolia is generally a safe country for travellers. In crowded places in Ulaanbaatar, watch out for pickpockets.
Distances are long and roads are often unpaved: travel times are slow, but part of the adventure.
There are guard dogs near gers: always follow your guide’s instructions.
